# AlignmentBundle { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle(
    id='',
    name=None,
    timelines=dict(),
    groups=dict(),
    meta=dict(),
    cross_group_claims=list(),
    cross_group_claim_fields=list(),
    support_policy=SupportPolicy.omit,
    styling=dict(),
    _warp_map_cache=dict(),
    _matchline_cache=dict(),
    _matchgraph_cache=dict(),
    _cache_claims_hash=0,
)
```

The primary entry point for all alignment workflows.

An AlignmentBundle manages timelines and their alignment relationships.
Within a group, coordinate transfer uses linear interpolation
(``TimelineGroup.get_coordinate_at()``). Across groups, transfer is mediated
by the ``MatchClaim`` → ``MatchLine`` → ``WarpMap`` pipeline.

The bundle provides:

- Timeline registration and lookup
- Group management (collections of perfectly aligned timelines)
- Coordinate transfer between any two timelines (same-group or
  cross-group via ``MatchClaim``/``WarpMap``)

IMPORTANT: The resulting bundle structure is order-independent. Adding
timelines in any order produces the same alignment relationships and
coordinate transfer results.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name                     | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| id                       | [str](`str`)                                                                           | Unique identifier for this bundle, ``bundle_N`` unless given.                                                                                                                  |
| name                     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Optional human-readable name.                                                                                                                                                  |
| timelines                | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), \'Timeline\'\]                                           | Dictionary mapping timeline IDs to Timeline objects: every timeline added, and the root of every one that is a child.                                                          |
| groups                   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [TimelineGroup](`timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup`)\] | Dictionary mapping group IDs to TimelineGroup objects. The groups are the one statement of membership; a timeline may be a member of several (see :attr:`timeline_to_groups`). |
| cross_group_claims       | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\]              | MatchClaims connecting timelines across groups (the per-claim Python-list store).                                                                                              |
| cross_group_claim_fields | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaimField](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaimField`)\]    | Columnar ``MatchClaimField`` stores of dense synchronous-instant pairwise claims, queried vectorized without materialising the full claim list.                                |
| styling                  | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]                                    | The members of the manifest's ``graphical`` other than ``order`` (``styles``, ``statements`` and any other), kept as given and never interpreted.                              |

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

The two claim stores are interchangeable as far as queries are
concerned: every reader consults both, so a bundle whose claims live
in a ``MatchClaimField`` answers exactly as a bundle holding the same
claims in the Python list.  What differs is cost — ``MatchClaimField``
queries stay vectorized, and ``get_claim_fields()`` is the accessor
that keeps them that way.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.alignment import AlignmentBundle
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
... )
>>> bundle = AlignmentBundle()
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=200))
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=91.0), grouped_with="clt_1"
... )
>>> stamp = bundle.get_matchstamp_at(100, "clt_1")
>>> stamp.get_coordinate_for("cpt_1", format="float")
45.5
```

### add_group { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_group }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_group(group)
```

Add a pre-built TimelineGroup with all its timelines at once.

This is the bulk-registration counterpart of ``add_timeline(..., as_group=...)``.
It registers the group and every timeline it contains — each under
its own ``id``, with the root of every member that is a child — into
the bundle's timeline and group registries. A member may already be a
member of another group of the bundle: a timeline may belong to
several groups.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                   | Description                                          | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| group  | [TimelineGroup](`timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup`) | A ``TimelineGroup`` that already contains timelines. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | self (for method chaining) |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the group's given ID is already held in the bundle (a minted one is minted again instead), or if a given id of a member's manifest tree is held by another timeline of the bundle (a minted id held there is minted again instead) or by a group. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Add a recording group with three DPTs:

    >>> grp = TimelineGroup(timelines=[dpt_1, dpt_2, dpt_3])
    >>> bundle.add_group(grp)

### add_match_claim_field { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_field }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_field(claim_field)
```

Add a columnar ``MatchClaimField`` of cross-group claims.

This is the columnar counterpart of :meth:`add_match_claims`.  The
field is stored as-is (one PyArrow struct column) and queried
vectorized by :meth:`get_matchstamp_at` /
:meth:`_get_or_build_matchgraph`, which filter the struct column and
materialise only the handful of claims at the queried coordinate.  A
dense whole-work field (on the order of a million claims) is therefore
never exploded into a Python list.

It complements the per-claim list path: a bundle may hold both a
Python-list ``cross_group_claims`` and one or more
``cross_group_claim_fields`` at once.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                              | Description                                                | Default    |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| claim_field | [MatchClaimField](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaimField`) | A :class:`MatchClaimField` of synchronous pairwise claims. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | self (for method chaining) |

### add_match_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_match_claims }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_match_claims(claims)
```

Add MatchClaims connecting timelines across different groups.

MatchClaims encode coordinate correspondences between timelines in
different groups (e.g., EEP recording notes matched to ABC score
notes).  They enable cross-group coordinate transfer via
``MatchLine`` → ``WarpMap``.

WarpMaps are built lazily on first ``transfer()`` or
``get_matchstamp_at()`` call, so adding claims is cheap.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                                                                                        | Default    |
|--------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| claims | [Any](`typing.Any`) | MatchClaim objects, claim tuples, or lists of claim tuples. A tuple is ``(timeline_a_id, interval_a, timeline_b_id, interval_b)``. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | self (for method chaining) |

### add_timeline { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_timeline }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.add_timeline(
    timeline,
    *,
    grouped_with=None,
    as_group=None,
)
```

Add a timeline, optionally grouped with an existing timeline.

This is the primary method for adding timelines to the bundle.
Timelines can be standalone or grouped with existing timelines.
Group membership makes timelines commensurable through
interpolation; it does not by itself assert any MatchClaim
between them. A member spans its whole group (see
:class:`~timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup`); to let only part of a
timeline participate, add the child covering that part.

A timeline is registered under its own ``id``. An ungrouped
participant is always a root: a child added without ``grouped_with``
or ``as_group`` registers its ROOT, and the child stays reachable as
the root's descendant (exactly what the dictionary form restores). A
child added to a group joins it, and its root joins the bundle as
well, ungrouped unless it is grouped itself.

A timeline may be a member of several groups: one already in the
bundle, grouped or not, joins a further group through
``grouped_with`` or ``as_group``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Default    |
|--------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline     | \'Timeline\'         | The Timeline to add.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | _required_ |
| grouped_with | [str](`str`) \| None | ID of an existing timeline to share a group with. If provided, both timelines become part of the same group. If the target timeline is not yet in a group, a new group is created with the target as its first member. A target in several groups is refused, since the group to join would be a guess. | `None`     |
| as_group     | [str](`str`) \| None | Name of the group if a new one is created. The new group's id is minted, ``group_N``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | self (for method chaining) |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the timeline is already in the bundle while no group is requested, or already in the group it would join; if ``grouped_with`` names a timeline of several groups; if a given id of its manifest tree — its own, its root's or any descendant's — is held by another timeline of the bundle (a minted id held there is minted again instead) or by a group. |
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If grouped_with references a non-existent timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Linear (full-extent) alignment:

    >>> from timetoalign.alignment import AlignmentBundle
    >>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
    ...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
    ...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
    ...     DiscreteLogicalTimeline,
    ... )
    >>> bundle = AlignmentBundle()
    >>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=4000))
    >>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
    ...     DiscreteLogicalTimeline(length=960), grouped_with="dgt_1"
    ... )
    >>> bundle.groups["group_1"].timeline_ids
    ['dgt_1', 'dlt_1']

Partial alignment: the participating part is a child.

    >>> image = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=300000)
    >>> holes = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=277776)
    >>> image.add_child(holes, offset=15343)
    >>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=600.0)
    >>> bundle = AlignmentBundle()
    >>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(audio, as_group="roll")
    >>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(holes, grouped_with="cpt_1")
    >>> sorted(bundle.timelines), bundle.timeline_to_groups
    (['cpt_1', 'dgt_1', 'dgt_2'], {'cpt_1': ('group_1',), 'dgt_2': ('group_1',)})

### are_commensurable { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.are_commensurable }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.are_commensurable(timeline_a, timeline_b)
```

Check if two timelines can be connected via transfer.

Two timelines are commensurable if groups connect them — they share
a group, or a chain of groups sharing members leads from one to the
other — or if a synchronous MatchClaim connects the timelines so
connected to each.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type         | Description         | Default    |
|------------|--------------|---------------------|------------|
| timeline_a | [str](`str`) | First timeline ID.  | _required_ |
| timeline_b | [str](`str`) | Second timeline ID. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                          |
|--------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if coordinates can be transferred between them. |

### create_match_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims(
    event_pairs,
    *,
    synchronous=True,
    agent='user',
    agent_identifier='manual',
)
```

Create MatchClaims from a list of event pairs.

Convenience factory for creating multiple MatchClaims from paired
events. Each tuple specifies two events and their timeline IDs.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                                                                                                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Default    |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| event_pairs      | [list](`list`)\[[tuple](`tuple`)\[[dict](`dict`) \| [str](`str`) \| None, [str](`str`), [dict](`dict`) \| [str](`str`) \| None, [str](`str`)\]\] | List of tuples, each containing: ``(event_a, timeline_a_id, event_b, timeline_b_id)``. ``event_a``/``event_b`` are each one of: an event dict (must have at least a ``start`` key with a coordinate; an ``end`` key on both sides produces an interval match), the ``id`` string of an existing event on the paired timeline (resolved via ``Timeline.get_event()``), or ``None``. Exactly one of ``event_a``/``event_b`` may be ``None``, producing a NOMATCH claim for the other side's event. The forms may be mixed within a pair. | _required_ |
| synchronous      | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                   | Whether the matches are temporally synchronous. Ignored for NOMATCH pairs, which are always non-synchronous.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `True`     |
| agent            | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                     | Name of the agent creating the claims (for provenance).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `'user'`   |
| agent_identifier | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                     | The agent's stable identifier — a version string for a software agent or a URI for a human agent (e.g. ``"manual"``, ``"dynamic_time_warping"``). Stored as ``Agent.identifier``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `'manual'` |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                      | Description                                                 |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | List of MatchClaim objects. Also automatically adds them to |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | the bundle's ``cross_group_claims``.                        |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If event dicts are missing required keys, an event id string doesn't resolve to an existing event, or both ``event_a`` and ``event_b`` are ``None``. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> pairs = [
...     ({"start": 0.0}, "score", {"start": 45.5}, "audio"),
...     ("note:000010", "score", "note:000042", "audio"),
...     ("note:000099", "score", None, "audio"),  # NOMATCH
... ]
>>> claims = bundle.create_match_claims(pairs, agent="manual_alignment")
>>> len(claims)
3
```

### from_bundles { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.from_bundles }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.from_bundles(bundles, *, id='', name=None)
```

Merge multiple bundles' groups, standalone timelines, and claims.

Registers every group and standalone timeline from each source
bundle into a new bundle, and carries over every cross-group
``MatchClaim`` (both the per-claim list and any columnar
``MatchClaimField`` stores) unchanged. Each source group is entered as
a new group with the same members, name and meta, each member keeping
its own lock; a minted group id is minted again in the merged bundle,
a given one is kept. Groups from
different source bundles remain distinct — merging does not itself
align timelines across bundles. Add cross-group MatchClaims (e.g. via
:meth:`create_match_claims`) afterwards to align them.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name    | Type                                  | Description                                           | Default    |
|---------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| bundles | [list](`list`)\[\'AlignmentBundle\'\] | The bundles to merge, in order.                       | _required_ |
| id      | [str](`str`)                          | Explicit ID for the merged bundle. Minted if omitted. | `''`       |
| name    | [str](`str`) \| None                  | Optional human-readable name for the merged bundle.   | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                              |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | A new AlignmentBundle containing every group, standalone |
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | timeline, and cross-group claim from ``bundles``.        |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If two source bundles share a given group ID, or a given timeline ID collision would occur across bundles. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> merged = AlignmentBundle.from_bundles([score_bundle, audio_bundle])
>>> merged.n_groups == score_bundle.n_groups + audio_bundle.n_groups
True
```

### from_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.from_dict }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.from_dict(data)
```

Read a bundle from any TimeSkeleton manifest.

The manifest's ``id`` becomes the bundle's (a manifest without ``id``,
named or anonymous, gives a bundle whose minted id :meth:`to_dict`
never writes), its ``name`` and ``meta`` the bundle's. Every root timeline is rebuilt;
each group is rebuilt from its ``Group`` object, its members resolved
among the roots and all their descendants and ordered by its
``graphical.order`` entry (``members`` order without one).
``graphical``'s other keys are kept as :attr:`styling`, and the
entries of ``graphical.order`` keyed by a timeline, its band orders,
are kept too, both unread. Every root no group names joins
ungrouped. A timeline several groups name is a member of each, one
object shared by them. Keys the library does not know are kept on the
object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written back.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description              | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|------------|
| data   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A TimeSkeleton manifest. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                              |
|--------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
|        | \'AlignmentBundle\' | The rebuilt bundle, without MatchClaims. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* is no TimeSkeleton manifest of version 0.7.0 or is malformed: a timeline id occurring twice, a group id occurring twice or equal to a timeline id, a member naming no timeline of ``"timelines"``, a group naming one member twice, a member that is an ancestor or descendant of another member of its group, an order that is no permutation of its group's members or names no group or timeline. The message names the problem. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.alignment import AlignmentBundle
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
... )
>>> bundle = AlignmentBundle(name="study")
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16)), as_group="score"
... )
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=40.0))
>>> data = bundle.to_dict()
>>> AlignmentBundle.from_dict(data).to_dict() == data
True
```

### get_claim_fields { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_claim_fields }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_claim_fields(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    between=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
```

Query the columnar claim stores, materialising nothing.

This is the scalable counterpart of :meth:`get_match_claims` for
bundles whose claims live in a ``MatchClaimField`` — a dense pairwise
alignment can hold hundreds of thousands of claims, and turning each
one into a Python object costs orders of magnitude more than the
columnar answer.  Every filter is applied as a vectorized PyArrow
mask, and the result is a list of *filtered fields*, one per store
that still has rows.

The filter parameters are exactly those of :meth:`get_match_claims`
and carry the same meaning.  Because a ``MatchClaimField`` holds
synchronous claims only, ``synchronous_only`` is a no-op here and
``nomatch_only`` returns nothing.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                   | Description                                                                | Default   |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| timeline_id      | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Keep claims involving this timeline ID.                                    | `None`    |
| timeline_ids     | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                   | Keep claims involving any of these timeline IDs.                           | `None`    |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Regex matched against timeline IDs via ``re.search()``.                    | `None`    |
| between          | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep claims connecting exactly these two timeline IDs (order-independent). | `None`    |
| synchronous_only | [bool](`bool`)                                         | No-op (every stored claim is synchronous).                                 | `False`   |
| nomatch_only     | [bool](`bool`)                                         | Returns an empty list.                                                     | `False`   |
| include_domains  | [set](`set`)\[\'Domain\'\] \| None                     | Only timelines in these domains.                                           | `None`    |
| include_units    | [set](`set`)\[\'TimeUnit\'\] \| None                   | Only timelines with these units.                                           | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                | Description                                                 |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaimField](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaimField`)\] | Filtered ``MatchClaimField`` objects, empty stores dropped. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> fields = bundle.get_claim_fields(timeline_id="rec-a:cpt_1")
>>> sum(len(f) for f in fields)
66780
```

### get_group { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_group }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_group(group_id)
```

Get a group by ID.

Supports partial string and regex matching:
1. Exact match: If ``group_id`` matches an ID exactly, returns it.
2. Substring match: If ``group_id`` is a substring of exactly one ID,
   returns that group. If multiple match, returns the first and warns.
3. Regex match: If ``group_id`` is a valid regex, matches via
   ``re.search()``. Same first-match logic with warning.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type         | Description                                                | Default    |
|----------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| group_id | [str](`str`) | The group's unique identifier, or a partial/regex pattern. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                   | Description               |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
|        | [TimelineGroup](`timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup`) | The TimelineGroup object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                      |
|--------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no group matches the pattern. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> bundle.get_group("group_1")          # Exact match
>>> bundle.get_group(r"_1$")             # Regex match
```

### get_match_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_match_claims }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_match_claims(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    between=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
```

Query MatchClaims connecting timelines across groups.

This is the primary interface for accessing alignment information.
All parameters are optional; when none are provided, returns all
claims.

Filters are combined with AND logic: a claim must satisfy every
non-None criterion. Uses the Unified Filter API.

Both claim stores are queried: the per-claim Python list and every
columnar ``MatchClaimField``. The columnar matches are filtered
vectorized but then **materialised**, one ``MatchClaim`` per surviving
row — for a dense pairwise alignment that is O(n) Python objects. Use
:meth:`get_claim_fields` when the columnar answer suffices, or narrow
the query first.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                   | Description                                                                                                               | Default   |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| timeline_id      | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Return claims involving this timeline ID.                                                                                 | `None`    |
| timeline_ids     | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                   | Return claims involving any of these timeline IDs.                                                                        | `None`    |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Regex pattern matched against timeline IDs via ``re.search()``. Example: ``r"^perf:"`` matches all performance timelines. | `None`    |
| between          | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`)\] \| None | Return claims connecting exactly these two timeline IDs (order-independent).                                              | `None`    |
| synchronous_only | [bool](`bool`)                                         | Exclude non-synchronous (NOMATCH) claims.                                                                                 | `False`   |
| nomatch_only     | [bool](`bool`)                                         | Return only non-synchronous (NOMATCH) claims.                                                                             | `False`   |
| include_domains  | [set](`set`)\[\'Domain\'\] \| None                     | Only timelines in these domains.                                                                                          | `None`    |
| include_units    | [set](`set`)\[\'TimeUnit\'\] \| None                   | Only timelines with these units.                                                                                          | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                      | Description                   |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | Filtered list of MatchClaims. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Get all synchronous claims for a performer::

    >>> claims = bundle.get_match_claims(
    ...     id_pattern=r"dlt_1$", synchronous_only=True
    ... )

Get NOMATCH claims for a specific pair::

    >>> nomatches = bundle.get_match_claims(
    ...     between=("score:clt_1", "perf:dlt_5"),
    ...     nomatch_only=True,
    ... )

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

### get_matchstamp_at { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_at }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_at(
    at,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    support_policy=None,
    conversion_maps=False,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
```

Get a cross-group match stamp for a position on a timeline.

Coordinate input is the primary interface for cross-domain coordinate
transfer and returns coordinates on every connected timeline. Interval
input resolves its endpoints through that same coordinate lane and
combines the two results.

A coordinate stamp is the **transitive cross-group union** reachable
from the query. Exact-anchor coordinates from the coordinate's
MatchGraph are overlaid first (exact wins over interpolated), then the
assembly walks outward across groups to closure: every reached timeline
expands into its own group (by interpolation) and warps into
not-yet-reached groups (by WarpMap). ``is_interpolated`` is ``False``
exactly when the query node itself carries an explicit anchor.

A timeline whose transferred coordinate falls outside alignment
support — the entering coordinate lies outside the transferring
WarpMap's source-anchor hull, or the produced coordinate would fall
outside ``[0, length]`` — is handled by ``support_policy``. No policy
ever yields a negative coordinate or one beyond a timeline's length.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Default    |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| [Interval](`timetoalign.core.Interval`) | The query position. Can be:  - int/float/Fraction: Raw value, ``timeline_id`` required. - Coordinate: Value with unit, ``timeline_id`` required. - IdCoordinate: Value with unit AND timeline_id   (``timeline_id`` param optional). - Interval: Two coordinate positions, ``timeline_id`` required.                               | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                           | ID of the source timeline. Required unless ``at`` is an ``IdCoordinate``, in which case the coordinate's own ``timeline_id`` is used.                                                                                                                                                                                              | `None`     |
| support_policy  | \'SupportPolicy \| str \| None\'                                                               | How to treat out-of-support timelines (``omit`` / ``clamp`` / ``extrapolate``). Accepts a :class:`~timetoalign.core.SupportPolicy` or its string name. ``None`` (the default) uses the bundle's ``support_policy`` setting, itself ``omit`` by default. The query timeline's own coordinate is never dropped, clamped, or altered. | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | \'ConversionMapsSpec\'                                                                         | C-map conversions available through unit lookup and display. Opt-in: defaults to ``False``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `False`    |
| timeline_ids    | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                           | Only include these timeline IDs in the result.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`     |
| id_pattern      | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                           | Regex filter for timeline IDs in the result.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `None`     |
| include_domains | [set](`set`)\[\'Domain\'\] \| None                                                             | Only these domains in the result.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `None`     |
| include_units   | [set](`set`)\[\'TimeUnit\'\] \| None                                                           | Only these units in the result.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                                             | Description                                                        |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`) \| [MatchIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchIntervalStamp`) | A coordinate query returns a MatchStamp. An Interval query returns |
|        | [MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`) \| [MatchIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchIntervalStamp`) | a MatchIntervalStamp combining its independently resolved endpoint |
|        | [MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`) \| [MatchIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchIntervalStamp`) | MatchStamps.                                                       |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                               |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If ``at`` is not a supported coordinate or Interval.      |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If timeline_id is None and ``at`` is not an IdCoordinate. |
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If timeline_id is not in the bundle.                      |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> ms = bundle.get_matchstamp_at(10.0, "score:clt_1")
>>> ms.n_timelines
23  # score + 22 performers
```

### get_matchstamp_table { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_table }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_table(
    at=None,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    claims=None,
    timeline_filter=None,
    from_graph=False,
    conversion_maps=False,
    format='table',
    fields=None,
    units=None,
)
```

Get a table of MatchStamps for alignment queries.

Analogous to ``get_timestamp_table()`` but for cross-group alignment.
Fields are timeline IDs holding their coordinate values; what a *row*
is depends on ``from_graph``:

- ``from_graph=False`` (default) — one row per synchronous claim.  A
  pairwise claim fills exactly two cells and leaves the rest null, so
  a dense pairwise alignment produces one sparse row per claim.
- ``from_graph=True`` — one row per connected component of the
  ``(timeline_id, coordinate)`` graph the claims induce.  The pairwise
  rows above collapse into the *cross-section* they describe: one row
  per aligned instant, every participating timeline filled.

When ``claims`` is None both claim stores are read: the per-claim
Python list and every columnar ``MatchClaimField``.  The columnar
stores are read four Arrow columns at a time — no ``MatchClaim`` is
ever materialised — which is what keeps a hundreds-of-thousands-of-rows
alignment tabulable.

When ``at`` is given instead of ``claims``, each position or event ID
is resolved through :meth:`get_matchstamp_at` and becomes exactly one
row — a full transitive cross-section, every reached timeline filled —
in input order. ``from_graph`` does not apply on this path (the stamps
are already collapsed cross-sections) and is ignored.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Default   |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| at              | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [Interval](`timetoalign.core.Interval`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [Interval](`timetoalign.core.Interval`)\] \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) \| None | Query positions or event IDs to resolve through :meth:`get_matchstamp_at`, one row each in input order. Each element is a raw ``int``/``float``/``Fraction`` or ``Coordinate`` (needing ``timeline_id``) or an ``IdCoordinate`` (carrying its own timeline). An ``Interval`` also needs ``timeline_id`` and has no table form. Mutually exclusive with ``claims``. | `None`    |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Source timeline for the ``at`` batch; may be ``None`` when every element is an ``IdCoordinate`` or an event ID. Ignored on the ``claims`` path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `None`    |
| claims          | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | List of MatchClaims to tabulate.  If None, uses every cross-group claim in the bundle (both stores).  When given, only those claims are tabulated.  Mutually exclusive with ``at``.                                                                                                                                                                                | `None`    |
| timeline_filter | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Only include these timeline fields.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `None`    |
| from_graph      | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Collapse claims into one row per connected component instead of one row per claim.  Ignored on the ``at`` path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `False`   |
| conversion_maps | \'ConversionMapsSpec\'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | C-map conversions to add as derived columns, one per (timeline, enabled unit-conversion map). Opt-in: defaults to ``False``. Only numeric unit-conversion maps (a ``target_unit`` set) become columns; label/structured maps appear in stamp display but never as table columns.                                                                                   | `False`   |
| format          | [TableFormat](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.TableFormat`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | ``"table"`` (default) for a PyArrow table, ``"dataframe"`` for a pandas DataFrame.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `'table'` |
| fields          | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | How to name the DataFrame fields (``format="dataframe"``).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `None`    |
| units           | [bool](`bool`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | If True (the DataFrame default), append units to field names like "name (unit)".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                         | Description                                                      |
|--------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'pa.Table \| pd.DataFrame\' | One field per timeline, each a coordinate struct carrying its    |
|        | \'pa.Table \| pd.DataFrame\' | number twice.  Non-synchronous claims are excluded.  Empty input |
|        | \'pa.Table \| pd.DataFrame\' | yields an empty table.                                           |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                            |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If both ``claims`` and ``at`` are given, on an unknown ``format``, or when a DataFrame-shaping option is supplied for an Arrow result. |

#### Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

Collapsed rows are ordered by the coordinate on the
lexicographically smallest timeline ID present in the component,
then by that ID — a total order, since two components can never
share a ``(timeline_id, coordinate)`` node.  A component that
somehow carries two coordinates for one timeline (which a
well-formed alignment never does) keeps the smaller one.

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> table = bundle.get_matchstamp_table()
>>> table.num_rows
100
>>> table.column_names
['score:clt_1', 'perf:dlt_1', 'perf:dlt_2', ...]
>>> bundle.get_matchstamp_table(from_graph=True).num_rows
25
>>> bundle.get_matchstamp_table([0.0, 50.0], "score:clt_1").num_rows
2
```

### get_matchstamps { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamps }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamps(
    claims=None,
    *,
    from_graph=True,
    conversion_maps=False,
)
```

Get MatchStamps for the bundle's claims.

The bare plural means "stamps for the claims this bundle holds" — it
is the claim-driven listing, not the batch sibling of
:meth:`get_matchstamps_at`. To resolve a batch of *positions*, use
:meth:`get_matchstamps_at`; to resolve event IDs, use
:meth:`get_matchstamps_for`.

Uses the bundle's caching mechanism for efficient retrieval.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Default   |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| claims          | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] \| None | List of MatchClaims to get stamps for. If None, uses every cross-group claim in the bundle — the per-claim list and every columnar ``MatchClaimField`` (see :meth:`get_match_claims`, which materialises the columnar rows). | `None`    |
| from_graph      | [bool](`bool`)                                                                    | If True (default), return full MatchStamps from the MatchGraph (all connected timelines). If False, return reduced 2-timeline stamps.                                                                                        | `True`    |
| conversion_maps | \'ConversionMapsSpec\'                                                            | C-map conversions available through unit lookup and display. Opt-in: defaults to ``False``.                                                                                                                                  | `False`   |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                     | Description                                                   |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`)\] | List of MatchStamp objects. Non-synchronous claims yield None |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`)\] | entries (filtered out).                                       |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> stamps = bundle.get_matchstamps()
>>> len(stamps)
100
>>> stamps[0].n_timelines
23
```

### get_matchstamps_at { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamps_at }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamps_at(
    at,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    support_policy=None,
    conversion_maps=False,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
```

Get cross-group MatchStamps at a collection of positions.

Every element is resolved through :meth:`get_matchstamp_at`, so each
one yields exactly one full transitive cross-section, and input order
is preserved.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [Interval](`timetoalign.core.Interval`)\] | Coordinate or Interval positions to resolve. Each element is a raw ``int``/``float``/``Fraction`` or ``Coordinate`` (needing ``timeline_id``), an ``IdCoordinate`` (carrying its own), or an ``Interval`` (needing ``timeline_id``). | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                              | ID of the source timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `None`     |
| support_policy  | \'SupportPolicy \| str \| None\'                                                                                                                                                                                                  | How to treat out-of-support timelines.                                                                                                                                                                                               | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | \'ConversionMapsSpec\'                                                                                                                                                                                                            | C-map conversions available through the stamps.                                                                                                                                                                                      | `False`    |
| timeline_ids    | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                              | Only include these timeline IDs in each result.                                                                                                                                                                                      | `None`     |
| id_pattern      | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Regex filter for timeline IDs in each result.                                                                                                                                                                                        | `None`     |
| include_domains | [set](`set`)\[\'Domain\'\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                | Only these domains in each result.                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `None`     |
| include_units   | [set](`set`)\[\'TimeUnit\'\] \| None                                                                                                                                                                                              | Only these units in each result.                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                                                               | Description                                                    |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`) \| [MatchIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchIntervalStamp`)\] | One stamp per input position. Coordinate elements produce      |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchStamp`) \| [MatchIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchIntervalStamp`)\] | MatchStamps and Interval elements produce MatchIntervalStamps. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> stamps = bundle.get_matchstamps_at([0.0, 50.0], "score:clt_1")
>>> stamps[1].get_coordinate_for("score:clt_1", format="float")
50.0
```

alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamps_for(

| include_domains | [set](`set`)\[\'Domain\'\] \| None                          | Only these domains in each result.                                                | `None`     |

### get_timeline { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_timeline }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_timeline(timeline_id)
```

Get a timeline by ID.

Supports partial string and regex matching:
1. Exact match: If ``timeline_id`` matches an ID exactly, returns it.
2. Substring match: If ``timeline_id`` is a substring of exactly one ID,
   returns that timeline. If multiple match, returns the first and warns.
3. Regex match: If ``timeline_id`` is a valid regex, matches via
   ``re.search()``. Same first-match logic with warning.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                                                   | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | The timeline's unique identifier, or a partial/regex pattern. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description          |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The Timeline object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                         |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no timeline matches the pattern. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> bundle.get_timeline("clt_1")          # Exact match
>>> bundle.get_timeline("score")         # Substring match
>>> bundle.get_timeline(r"^perf:")       # Regex match
```

### get_timelines { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_timelines }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_timelines(ids)
```

Get multiple timelines by their IDs.

Convenience method for retrieving several timelines at once.
Each ID supports partial string and regex matching (via
``get_timeline()``).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                       | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|------------|
| ids    | [list](`list`)\[[str](`str`)\] | List of timeline IDs (or partial/regex patterns). | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                  |
|--------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[\'Timeline\'\] | List of Timeline objects in the same order as the input IDs. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                      |
|--------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If any timeline ID is not found. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> timelines = bundle.get_timelines(["score", "audio", "midi"])
>>> len(timelines)
3
```

### summary { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.summary }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.summary()
```

Get a summary of the bundle contents.

Returns a deterministic representation suitable for comparison.
Keys and timeline lists are sorted for order-independence.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                         |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Dictionary with bundle information. |

### to_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.to_dict }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.to_dict(
    minimal=False,
    events=False,
    external_references=False,
)
```

Write the bundle as a TimeSkeleton manifest.

The manifest carries the bundle's ``id`` only when one was given
(a minted id is never written), its ``name`` and ``meta``, every
root timeline of the bundle — every registered timeline that is no
child, which includes the root of each one that is — as
:meth:`Timeline.to_dict <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.to_dict>`
writes it, sorted by id, and the groups sorted by id, each naming its
members by id. ``graphical.order`` keeps every group's member order
under its id and, unchanged, the band order read with the manifest
of every timeline written, beside the members of :attr:`styling`. A
root no group names is ungrouped. MatchClaims are not written; the
support policy is a setting of the bundle, not part of the manifest.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                | Type           | Description                                        | Default   |
|---------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| minimal             | [bool](`bool`) | If True, leave out every key at its default value. | `False`   |
| events              | [bool](`bool`) | Write every timeline's event rows.                 | `False`   |
| external_references | [bool](`bool`) | Write every timeline's external references.        | `False`   |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                     |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | ``{"timeskeleton": "0.7.0", "id"?, "name", "meta", "timelines": |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | [...], "groups": [...], "graphical"?: {"order": {...}, ...}}``. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.alignment import AlignmentBundle
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
... )
>>> bundle = AlignmentBundle()
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16)), as_group="score"
... )
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=40.0), grouped_with="clt_1"
... )
>>> data = bundle.to_dict()
>>> "id" in data, [timeline["id"] for timeline in data["timelines"]]
(False, ['clt_1', 'cpt_1'])
>>> data["groups"]
[{'id': 'group_1', 'name': 'score', 'meta': {}, 'members': ['clt_1', 'cpt_1']}]
>>> data["graphical"]["order"]
{'group_1': ['clt_1', 'cpt_1']}
```

### transfer { #timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.transfer }

```python
alignment.AlignmentBundle.transfer(coord, from_timeline, to_timeline)
```

Transfer a coordinate from one timeline to another.

Automatically determines the conversion path:

1. If both timelines are in the same group: typed group retrieval.
2. If in different groups with MatchClaims: builds a ``MatchLine``
   and a cached ``WarpMap`` and calls it to
   interpolate the coordinate.
3. If no path exists: returns ``None``.

Low-level coordinate transfer utility. For user-facing coordinate
queries, use ``get_matchstamp_at()`` which returns a full cross-section
as a MatchStamp.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                                | Description                       | Default    |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------|
| coord         | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | The coordinate value to transfer. | _required_ |
| from_timeline | [str](`str`)                                        | ID of the source timeline.        | _required_ |
| to_timeline   | [str](`str`)                                        | ID of the target timeline.        | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description                                            |
|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [float](`float`) \| None | The transferred coordinate, or None if no path exists. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                              |
|--------|------------------------|------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If either timeline is not in the bundle. |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}
